If rock unit D is an intrusion, which geologic principle would you use to determine the age of rock unit D with respect to rock unit E (the fault)? 

This is a declarative sentence.

To determine the age of rock unit D with respect to rock unit E, we would use the principle of cross-cutting relationships. Since rock unit D is an intrusion, it cuts across rock unit E, which is a fault. The principle of cross-cutting relationships states that an intrusion or fault cuts across older rocks, so if rock unit D cuts across rock unit E, it must be younger than rock unit E.
